roles.unit_id: state (numeric ID 1-39; README: no state names, state 3 = California)
roles.outcome: cigsale (per-capita cigarette SALES, packs/person/year - not consumption)
roles.treatment_group: california (True only for state 3, all 31 years)
roles.time_indicator: after_treatment (True for year >= 1989 in ALL 39 states - a year dummy, NOT the treatment)

sources.unit: data/README.md: numeric state IDs 1-39; treated unit is California = state 3 (california == True for all 31 rows of state 3)
sources.outcome: data/README.md + plan.md: cigsale = per-capita cigarette SALES in packs/person/year (not consumption)
sources.treatment_start: plan.md + data/README.md: Proposition 99, 25-cent tax effective 1 Jan 1989; treatment = california AND year >= 1989
sources.after_treatment_note: after_treatment is a year dummy (year >= 1989) for every state, NOT the treatment. Per my procedure I did not adopt it as the treatment before checking: 02_design_checks.py verifies it is True in 456 control state-year rows, so it fails the check and is rejected.
sources.controls_covariates: plan.md: no covariates (lnincome/beer/age15to24 missing in many years, would drop rows; AGENTS.md forbids adding them without asking)
sources.cluster: unit = state, default; but only 1 treated unit, so clustered SEs are not reliable and inference relies on placebo tests (see summary)
sources.reference_period: plan.md: 1988 as event-study reference (last pre-treatment year)
sources.mechanism_outcome: plan.md mechanism check: retprice (retail price per pack); no missing values (data/README.md)
